Commentary.Commentary: So we're done with this one. South Africa carry their good form from the ODI series forward and win this opening T20I. Zimbabwe were let down by their batting order again and as a result, lost their 9th successive game in T20Is. They will want to rectify that quickly and win the next game to keep the series alive. It takes place on 12th October, at 1800 local (1600 GMT). Join in for that. Cheers!

South Africa skipper, Faf du Plessis, says he believed the score they had on the board was enough as the wicket was a bit on the slower side. Reckons the ball didn't grip as much in the first innings, so they were able to get some partnerships in the middle. Praises van der Dussen and Miller for their partnership and adds both are quality players. Feels Imran Tahir has a knack for taking wickets so he used him upfront which paid off. Further adds they didn't expect so much dew, so it became a bit challenging for the wrist spinners, but them and his pacers bowled really well despite that. Continues saying that even when Peter Moor was scoring big, he knew one wicket could bring about a turnaround.

Man of the Match, Imran Tahir, says he's really pleased with his bowling and is honoured to play for his country, so doesn't take anything for granted. Is glad he executed his plans to perfection and happy that he's able to help the team. Mentions that he practices a lot with the new ball in the nets and puts in a lot of hard work. States he's a big believer in the fact that it's never too late to learn (bowling with the new ball), so will just give it his best.

Zimbabwe skipper, Hamilton Masakadza, says 160 was just about par and he thought his team could have chased it down. Credits his bowlers for restricting South Africa to 160 and bowling well. Admits his batting unit needs work and is the area they need to work on. Applauds Peter Moor's batting effort but is disappointed he couldn't finish it off. Ends by saying they'll try to do better in the next game.

Imran Tahir was the man who lead the charge with his second 5-wicket haul in T20Is. Barring Shamsi, who got hit for plenty (especially where he conceded 24 against Moor in one over), everyone else did well and contributed with the wickets. It was a rather good performance from the home side, even if it wasn't perfect, as it got them the win. Earlier, some fine batting from du Plessis, Miller and debutant van der Dussen (who scored a fifty), helped the Proteas put up 160 on the board which proved to be more than enough. Stay tuned for the presentation...

South Africa manage to hold on, but nobody can say they weren't given a run for their money tonight. They started off well with the ball after setting a target of 161 and scalped early wickets, then continued with more. Had it not been for Moor and Mavuta's quickfire 50-stand, this game would have been over much early. The pair added some fast runs, threatened to take this close, but once the partnership was broken it was a mere formality after that.

OUT! And there it is! Game over. SOUTH AFRICA WIN BY 34 RUNS! Phehlukwayo pitches it full on off, Moor looks to clear long off with a lofted shot but can't get under it cleanly. Jonker out in the deep moves to his right and takes a good catch. The hosts take a 1-0 lead in the series.
Fuller and slower wide outside off, Moor fails to connect.
Andile Phehlukwayo returns to the attack.

What just happened here? A misfield and that was almost a boundary. Yikes! It's the magic man Imran Tahir. Yorker on off, Mpofu digs it out down towards third man. It's rolling there slowly, Tahir bends to takes it but the ball takes an odd bounce in front of him and goes through his legs. He runs back and pulls it back inside the rope just in time. Saves some embarrassment for himself, even if it just a little. No run taken.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Chris Mpofu is the last batsman in for Zimbabwe.

OUT! Ngidi is never too far away from the wickets, is he? Angles in a fierce length ball on leg, it keeps coming in with the angle and catches Jarvis on the thigh pad as he looks to flick it away. It deflects back onto the off stump and uproots it. The end for Zimbabwe now?
Full ball, it's driven down to long off for a single.

Jarvis was expecting the short ball but Ngidi still got him on the helmet. Was sharp, angled in, with good pace. On middle and leg, Kyle ducked but still caught one on the helmet. Oooff! A leg bye is taken as the ball goes on the off side.
Banged in short, Jarvis somehow manages to let it be.
Wide! This one is down the leg side, Jarvis looks to put bat on ball but fails to do so.
Kyle Jarvis strides out to the middle. 38 needed off 24. Still some last twist left in this game? Lungi Ngidi to bowl now.

OUT! GONE! Of all the deliveries, this is the poorest one he's bowled in the entire over. Mavuta will feel hard done by this. He'd have wanted to sent it sailing once more. Full toss well outside off, Brandon reaches out to it and slices it straight to Ngidi at third man. The catch is taken. The umpire wants to check the front foot no ball and the height as well, both are okay and Mavuta has to make the long walk back.
Top edged but safe! Shortish in length, Brandon pulls and it goes off the edge through square leg. A couple taken.

SIX! Oh, dear! This is turning into some game now. Unreal stuff. Junior Dala angles it in on middle and leg, Mavuta goes across the line and lifts it ever so well over square leg. Clears the boundary rope, along with the leaping fielder and earns a biggie. The 50-run stand is up too, in just 17 balls.
The ball has been changed. Not sure what the reason is, but the umpire doesn't seem quite pleased it.
Length delivery around off, Mavuta gets an inside edge to square leg. Big gap out there, so he's able to come back for the second.

FOUR! 33 runs off the last 8 balls. South Africa are bleeding runs here. Dala errs in line and bowls it down leg, all Mavuta has to do is get some bat on it. He goes, beats a diving Quinton de Kock and finds the fine leg fence.
FOUR! Shot. Short and outside off, Mavuta rises on his toes, gets on top of the bounce and crunches it through the covers for a boundary.
Junior Dala comes back on to bowl.

SIX! Oh, yes it is! Wow. 25 runs off the over, could this be the game-changer? Surely? Shamsi flights this up around off, Moor picks up the length early and gets low quickly. Slog sweeps this hard and sends it deep into the mid-wicket stands for half a dozen.

SIX! Make that three! This is some superb hitting. Wow. In line of the stumps, Moor is onto the back foot again and muscles this over mid-wicket. Into the stands and that's another biggie. Fourth one incoming?
SIX! Two in two from Peter Moor. This is good, clean hitting. It's full, loopy and right in his slot, he puts his front foot forward, gets close to the pitch and slogs it over mid-wicket.
SIX! Dropped short and Moor dispatches this. Rocks back instantly, swings it with all his might and clears the square leg boundary for a maximum.
Short ball, pulled away into the leg side for a run.
Another attempt for a reverse sweep, another miss. Mavuta is low to hit it away but it spins away and he misses.
Tabraiz Shamsi is brought back on.
Single to end the over as Mavuta knocks it to long on. That brings an end to Tahir's spell. He finishes with figures of 4-0-23-5.
Another audacious effort. Sensational. Tahir loops it up on middle and leg, Mavuta looks to play the reverse sweep but fails to connect and gets hit on the pads.
Works it down in front of mid-wicket for no run.

SIX! NAILED IT! Brandon Mavuta taking the attack to Imran Tahir. Takes some courage, that. He shows all three stumps even before the ball is released, it's the googly but he doesn't care. Just swips it across the line and clears the mid-wicket rope. Amazing hit.
Not much foot movement from PJ Moor. Tossed up leg break on off, it's wristed down to long on from within the crease. The batsmen change ends.
Quicker googly on middle and leg, Mavuta backs away and goes inside out. Clears the infield over covers and takes one for it.
A short delivery which has been pulled away. They pick up a single.
Brandon Mavuta walks out now.

OUT! Soft dismissal. Bumper banged in around off, Chisoro rocks onto the back foot and awkwardly mistimes the pull aerially towards the bowler. Phehlukwayo moves a little to his left and takes a dolly. Simplest of wickets, really.
Through backward square leg again, two more runs result.
Length ball around leg, goes off Chisoro's pads as he attempts to work it away on the leg side. It rolls away behind square leg and a couple of leg byes are taken.
On the shorter side of things, outside off, Chisoro throws his bat at that but misses.
Short of a length outside off, cut square through point for a single.
Andile Phehlukwayo back into the attack.
No hat-trick. But a superb delivery nonetheless. Brings out the wrong 'un again as he bowls it on off, Chisoro doesn't have a clue about it and gets beaten past the outside edge.
Tendai Chisoro is out to bat.

FOUR! Second T20I 5-fer. Imran Tahir on fire here tonight and he's on a hat-trick for the second time in this innings. Lands the googly outside off and it spins back in sharply. Chigumbura is half-forward to block but is caught on the front pad. Loud appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Was clean plumb.
Elton Chigumbura is the new man in.

FOUR! Fourth one of the night for Tahir. He becomes the leading wicket-taker for South Africa in T20Is, going past Dale Steyn. He loops up a lovely leg spinner on the stumps, Williams jumps out to put this away but misses the line altogether. Gets beaten past the outside and hears the death rattle behind. The leggie is on song.
Leans ahead and drives it down to long on for another one.
Shorter this time, punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Bit full, hit down to long on for one run.
Imran Tahir returns.
Swing and a miss! Going away from the right-hander, on a shorter length, Moor is on the back foot to heave it away. It goes past the bat and into the keeper's gloves.
The reverse sweep. Sean is on one knee and brooms it away to sweeper cover to change ends.
The googly around off, Moor stands firm and looks to go big downtown. Can only lift it towards long off on the bounce. Single collected.
Leg spinner around off, Williams gets low and brings out the sweep, gets it off the inner half behind square leg. One more to the total.
Quicker one outside off, forced through to sweeper cover for a run.
Loopy and spinning away from outside off, Williams gets low and drags the slog sweep to deep mid-wicket for a single.
SIX! HUGE! What a strike! Overpitched ball on off, Moor extends his arms and deposits this over mid-wicket for the first maximum of the innings.
Length ball on leg, Williams hits it in the gap through mid-wicket to give his partner the strike.
Moor works it down the leg side. They pick up a single. Smart.
FOUR! 50 up for Zimbabwe and a good shot to get there. Fuller ball outside off, with mid off up he lofts it over him and that was always going to the fence. Need more of this.
Length again on middle and leg, punched to mid on. Zimbabwe need to at least rotate the strike.
Back of a length ball on off, defended off the back foot.
Another reverse sweep. Gets into position early and reverse sweeps it but straight to the man at point.
Leg spinner on leg, lofted over mid-wicket for a run.
Full and on off, it's been driven superbly through the covers. They manage to come back for the second.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Uses his feet and flicks this through mid-wicket for a brace.
The batsman has driven it straight back to the bowler.
Peter Moor is next in.

OUT! What a catch! Pick that out! Short ball which cramps Taylor for room. He still looks to guide it towards third man but gets a thick edge which flies towards de Kock. Quinton moves to his left, dives and takes the catch with his left hand. Great stuff and some good keeping. Zimbabwe lose another wicket and need more 121 runs to win.
Outside off, Taylor gets a bottom edge to the keeper.
Length outside off, Taylor cuts it but a good effort from the debutant, Rassie, saves his team the runs.
Good running. Hit far from the fielder at mid on and immediately sets off for the run.
Williams gets an inside edge and the ball hits him on the pads.
Full on middle and leg, hit through mid on and jogs to get to the other end.
Change of ends for Junior Dala.
Single to end the over. Hit towards mid-wicket and will retain the strike for the next over.
Wide! Short ball down leg. Taylor looks to pull but it is way down leg.
Plays it through the mid-wicket region and gets to the other end.
Reverse sweep again and this time gets it past the backward point region. Only just though. Enough time to come back for the second.
Stays inside and flicks this behind square for a run.
Good shot but straight to the man at backward point. Picks up the ball early and reverse sweeps it to that region.
Stifled appeal which dies. Pitched outside leg, Taylor looks to flick but gets hit on his back leg. Also, going down leg that.
Wide! Down the leg side to start with. Straighter one down leg, Taylor leaves it alone.
Tabraiz Shamsi is called to bowl.

Close but makes it. Plays this with soft hands towards mid-wicket and hares to the other end. The fielder goes for a direct hit but misses the stumps. One run added to the total. 31/3 in the Powerplay, as compared to South Africa's 52/2.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR! Short ball down the leg side, Taylor looks to pull this but gets a top edge which flies towards the fine leg region for back-to-back boundaries.
FOUR! SHOT! Clears his front leg and carves this to the off side for a boundary. Full in length around off, Taylor makes room and finds the gap through cover-point.
Fuller in length this time on leg. Taylor defends this with a straight bat to the on side.
Starts off with a slower one on a back of a length. He angles this into the batsman. Taylor looks to flick it away but misses it completely.
Andile Phehlukwayo to bowl now.

Dropped! Tough chance though. Just behind a length, angling across from around off, Williams hits this back aerially towards the bowler. Dala sticks his hands out to his right, but can't keep a hold of it. Just hit too hard.

FOUR! Shot. Pure timing from Sean Williams. Fullish in length around off, the left-hander drives it past mid off with the full face of the bat. Shamsi lazily tries to chase it down, but can't stop it. A boundary results.
Coming back in on a bit of a fuller length, Williams comes ahead to push it down the ground but gets an inside edge back onto his pads.
Sharp bumper. Around off, going away and not much room for Williams to do anything about it. He can only let it go past him.
Stays behind the line of this one and defends solidly.
Fraction straight in line, Taylor works it off his pads away on the leg side for a single.
Junior Dala is into the attack.
Leg spinner on off, driven to mid off. What a terrific over from the spinner, 6 runs and 2 wickets from it.
Full on leg, milked away through mid-wicket to get to the other end.
The batsman has driven it through mid on. One run added to the total.
FOUR! No hat-trick and no pressure shown from Williams. Full ball on off, Sean gets low and drives this through covers for a good looking boundary.
Sean Williams is the next man in. He's so excited to get in that he doesn't even wait for Musakanda to come towards the dugout. The southpaw will face the hat-trick ball.

OUT! Imran Tahir is on a hat-trick! Brilliant bowling this. Musakanda makes a comeback to the Zimbabwe team and is out first ball. Googly which is dragged down on off. It spins in, Tarisai is early into his shot as he looks to turn it to the on side. Gets an inside edge onto his thigh pads which goes back behind on the leg side. De Kock moves to his left, dives and takes a good catch.
Tarisai Musakanda is the new man in.

OUT! Tahir gets another one! Googly and traps the skipper in front of the stumps. Tossed up middle, the ball spins in and hits Masakadza on the leg as he gets low to swipe the ball. He puts in an appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Zimbabwe lose both their openers within 4 overs.
Looks to get it past point again but cuts it to the man at point.
FOUR! Finally! This one is a bit full and on middle and off. Taylor gives room and carves it past backward point for a boundary. The first one of the chase.
Once again. Thrice in 4 balls now. Similar ball and Taylor cannot get it past point.
Length outside off, Taylor cannot find the gap and gives it to point.
Outside off again, cut to point.
Short ball outside off, Taylor gets a bottom edge to that to the slip cordon. Should have looked to cut that away.
Leg spinner outside off, Masakadza looks to cut it but fails to put bat to ball.
Taylor has flicked the ball off his pads. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Brendan Taylor is in at no.3.

OUT! Tahir draws first blood. How often have you seen a spinner bowl a yorker and get a wicket? Bowls this one full on off and yorks Chibhabha. The batsman tries to get his bat down but not in time. Off go the bails and Tahir is up and running.

Two Wides. Misses his line again and bowls this down the leg side. Masakadza looks to sweep it but cannot get bat to ball. De Kock cannot take it cleanly. The ball rolls down to fine leg as they steal a run.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads. One run added to the total.
Strays on the legs again, Masakadza milks it through mid on for a single.
Leg spinner on leg, flicked away through square leg for one.
Imran Tahir to bowl from the other end.
Good start for South Africa. Just the one run off it. Back of a length ball outside off, punched off the back foot.
Short ball outside off, Masakadza looks to cut it but gets a bottom edge, one bounce to the first slip fielder.
Back of a length ball around off, Hamilton punches it down to mid off.
Change up straigthaway from Lungi. Bowls a cutter outside off, Masakadza leaves it alone.
Length outside off, Chibhabha opens the bat face and guides it to third man to get off the mark.
Comes in from over the wicket and lands it full on middle and off, Chibhabha drives it to mid off.

We have had a 10- minute delay. The groundsmen had taken a last minute call to dry up the outfield due to the moisture. But, we are all set to get the run chase underway now. Hamilton Masakadza and Chamu Chibhabha will open for the visitors while Lungi Ngidi will take the new ball.
